hero.title: Stories of Madurai
hero.description: A city shaped by kings, temples, literature, trade and tradition.

intro.heading: A City Written Into History
paragraphs: Madurai's story stretches back over two thousand years, shaped by dynasties, scholars and traders who built one of South India's most enduring cities.
Madurai's story is not limited to monuments. Its history continues through its streets, festivals, food, language and traditions.

timeline.title: Early Madurai
timeline.desc: Formation of an important cultural and trading centre on the banks of the Vaigai.

timeline.title: Literature & Trade
timeline.desc: A flourishing hub of Tamil literature, poetry and long-distance trade.

timeline.title: Royal Madurai
timeline.desc: Capital of the Pandya dynasty, celebrated for its temples and governance.

timeline.title: Architecture & Palaces
timeline.desc: Grand palaces and temple towers built under Thirumalai Nayak's rule.

timeline.title: A Changing City
timeline.desc: New administration and infrastructure reshaped daily life in Madurai.

timeline.title: Living Heritage
timeline.desc: A thriving city where ancient traditions continue alongside modern life.

rulers.name: Kulasekara Pandyan
rulers.desc: Credited with laying the early foundations of Madurai as a capital city.

rulers.name: Thirumalai Nayak
rulers.desc: Commissioned the iconic palace and expanded the Meenakshi Temple complex.

rulers.name: Rani Mangammal
rulers.desc: A respected regent known for public works, roads and rest houses.

architecture.name: Meenakshi Temple
architecture.desc: A masterpiece of Dravidian temple architecture, rebuilt over centuries.

architecture.name: Nayak Palace
architecture.desc: Indo-Saracenic grandeur commissioned by Thirumalai Nayak in 1636.

architecture.name: Gandhi Museum
architecture.desc: Once a queen's palace, now home to India's freedom struggle history.

architecture.name: Heritage Sites
architecture.desc: Pillared halls and mandapams that still shape daily city life.

facts.text: Madurai has been an important centre of Tamil culture and literature for centuries.
The city is often called the 'Athens of the East' for its Sangam-era literary legacy.
Meenakshi Temple's gopurams are covered in over 33,000 sculptures.

closing.title: The story of Madurai is still being written.
closing.description: Walk through its streets, taste its flavours, meet its traditions and become part of the story.
